description.narrative: 1. Provide 8 advanced life support flight qualified paramedics to provide 24/7 emergency medical intervention to UN and INGO staff (and in extremis support to partners and donors). 2. Provide an emergency medical officer to be located in Kabul to support and coordinate medical emergency intervention with aero-medical evacuation of injured or ill UN and INGO staff. 3. Emergency Medical courses will be conducted by the MERT personnel as part of their normal duties (at no additional cost) it is expected that Two (2) Training sessions should be provided at each location per month; one will involve capacity building for major health institutions in medical procedures and one will be general first aid training to UN and INGO staff in each location. 4. Mass casualty plans for all UN compounds will be reviewed by the MERT personnel and where possible rehearsals will be conducted of the plans. 5. The MERT personnel should assist the major medical facilities (hospitals or medical centres) in their location to review mass casualty response preparedness and response capacity, develop/review mass casualty plans and provide training to the emergency staff and facility managers on mass casualty preparedness and response. 6. All medical staff must be fluent in English (oral and written) 7. Reporting: the United Nations will require monthly reports on MERT / Medical Officer activities. These should be submitted with in conjunction with invoices.

De internationella stridande trupperna har de senaste åren minskat sin närvaro i Afghanistan, därmed försvinner också mycket av den kvalificerade akutsjukvården. Insatsen täcker delvis upp för den förlusten och erbjuder FN personal, humanitär personal, internationella NGOs, samt även internationella givare tillgång till MERT team (Medical Emergancy Response Team) i följande städer - Gardiz, Lashkar Gah, Herat, Jalalabad, Mazar, Fayzabad, Maimana och Bamyan.
MERT erbjuder 8 flygplan med kvalificerad ambulanspersonal med specialiserad och avancerad akutsjukvård inom de första kritiska 72 timmarna. Vidare erbjuder MERT team utbildning inom akutsjukvård till de största befintliga hälsovårdsinrättningarna, samt utbildning i första hjälpen till FN-personal och internationella NGOs på plats i ovan nämnda städer. MERT har dessutom en samordnare inom akutsjukvård stationerad i Kabul. MERT är uppbyggd efter en modell som tidigare har testats i Somalia.
Medical Emergency Response Team (MERT) Trauma Care, Stabilisation and Medevac Support

The project’s accomplishments over the project period including medical response interventions, training, assessment of hospitals and support to different kinds of field missions. The donor supported MERT project was a gap filling project. The MERT is now taken over by UN through a cost sharing between UNAMA and non-UNAMA (UNCT funds and RCO / CHF funds).
